title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: E is an elliptic curve over a field k of characteristic ≠ 2, with full 2-torsion rational (the ε_i). The previous page realised ℘ : E → P^1_k as the quotient by ±1 with ℘(0_E) = ∞, so ℘ is determined up to affine maps. The ξ_i = ℘(ε_i) are the finite branch points.

On this page Grothendieck does the following.

(1) He writes the cubic whose roots are ξ_1, ξ_2, ξ_3: z^3 + a_1 z^2 + a_2 z + a_3 = Π(z − ξ_i), equation (60). The a_α are the signed elementary symmetric functions of the ξ_i.

(2) He chooses a basis δ of the tangent space t_E = T_{E,0}, tied to ℘ modulo constants (modulo k·1) by ε_2(℘) ≅ δ^{⊗2}. Here ε_2(℘) is the leading polar term of ℘ at 0, viewed in t_E^{⊗2}. He sets ℘' = θ_δ ℘, the derivation attached to the invariant vector field δ. One then gets the Weierstrass relation ℘'^2 = ℘^3 + a_1 ℘^2 + a_2 ℘ + a_3. The normalisation has no factor 4, which a suitable choice of δ achieves in characteristic ≠ 2.

(3) He computes the involution σ_i of P^1 induced on E/{±1} by translation x ↦ x + ε_i. Translation by ε_i commutes with −1, so it descends. It swaps ∞ (the image of 0) with ξ_i, and swaps ξ_j with ξ_k. Write σ_i z = (az + b)/(cz + d) with c = 1. The conditions σ_i ∞ = ξ_i and σ_i ξ_i = ∞ give a = ξ_i and d = −ξ_i. The condition σ_i ξ_j = ξ_k gives b = ξ_j ξ_k − ξ_i(ξ_j + ξ_k).

Equivalently, σ_i z = ξ_i + (ξ_i − ξ_j)(ξ_i − ξ_k)/(z − ξ_i). This is the classical formula x(P + T) for a 2-torsion point T.

Purpose: the next page computes the fixed points of σ_i. These are the x-coordinates of points P with P + ε_i = −P, i.e. 2P = ε_i, which are 4-torsion points. This feeds the explicit description of level structures and moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, the subject of the whole cote.
errors: No errors on this page. The formula for b checks: ξ_i^2 + b = (ξ_i − ξ_j)(ξ_i − ξ_k), as it should be.
Gap continued on the next page: rewriting b_i as −(a_2 + 2a_3/ξ_i) requires ξ_i ≠ 0. Grothendieck flags this himself in a margin note there.
Minor: the condition σ_i ξ_k = ξ_j is not checked separately. It follows automatically because σ_i is an involution (trace a + d = 0).

ideas.what: Weierstrass equation with roots ξ_i at the 2-torsion points, derived intrinsically. The derivation uses an invariant differential/vector field δ ∈ t_E and the identification of the polar part of ℘ with δ^{⊗2}.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre/Weierstrass normal form with full level-2 structure; normalisation by an invariant differential (as in Katz–Mazur)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass; the intrinsic modular version is due to Deligne–Rapoport and Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Explicit Möbius involution on P^1 = E/±1 induced by translation by a 2-torsion point: σ_i z = ξ_i + (ξ_i − ξ_j)(ξ_i − ξ_k)/(z − ξ_i).
ideas.modern_name: Translation by 2-torsion on the Kummer line; x-coordinate formula for P + T (cf. Vélu's formulas)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (19th century); standard textbook exercise (e.g. Silverman)

ideas.what: Setting up the computation of the fixed points of σ_i, i.e. the halves of ε_i (4-torsion points), on the Kummer line.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but entirely classical computation: the Weierstrass form with full 2-torsion and the Möbius involution induced by translation by a 2-torsion point. Its only distinctive feature is the intrinsic normalisation via δ ∈ t_E. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The equation number read as '(10)' is almost certainly '(60)'. It follows (59) on the previous page and precedes (61) on the next.
'liée à ℘ mod h.1' should likely read 'mod k.1': ℘ is determined modulo additive constants in k.
The struck-out line under the brace is the explicit product '(z−ξ_1)(z−ξ_2)(z−ξ_3)', replaced by Π_i(z−ξ_i).
In 'qui {+s'identifie+}' the insertion reads 's'identifie à', replacing struck-out text.
The denominator in the final displayed formula is 'ξ_j − ξ_i', as the image shows.
